conclusion: The documented WAC 001 outcome f6h5/661/d12 is the h256_e12 lock net's own observation (B_lock: f6h5 cp 661).
tests.cpp accepts the 6.4.24 expectation (g3g6 mate) or exactly the documented horizon outcome; any other failing outcome prints PIN_MISMATCH and keeps the two ordinary FAIL lines.
f019-f022 find the mate at d12 (g3g6 mate 2), so the pin is never consulted for them.
f023 is the only candidate that, like the lock, plays the horizon move f6h5 at d12, but with its own evaluation: 620 cp in every run (v3, CI v4 x2, CI v5, ASan build, UCI Hash 8).

Root cause: a net-specific pin applied to a different net. Not a tool, engine or flakiness defect. Remedy (proposal only, not applied): a REVIEWED per-net pin entry for f023 (allowlist pins with exact_lines) or re-recorded pins if f023 ever became the lock; v4/v5 already wrote the UNREVIEWED 661 -> 620 proposal.
